fatal_errors: The proposed twinning-mediated mechanism directly conflicts with the target result, in which deformation proceeds through Shockley partials and stacking faults without twinning.
It replaces the target FeNiCrMn single-crystal molecular-dynamics comparison across orientation, temperature, and strain rate with a processing-dependent CoCrFeNi experiment.
Annealing is not a clean manipulation of compositional heterogeneity because it can also change local chemical order, defect density, grain structure, and residual stress.
explanation: The hypothesis is scientifically plausible and is directly supported by E1 for room-temperature, <110>-oriented, single-crystalline CoCrFeNi nanopillars. Its same-composition processing comparison and explicit falsification rule are reasonably discriminating, although independent quantification of chemical heterogeneity and generalized stacking-fault-energy distributions would be needed to establish mediation. It is not a reconstruction of the hidden target: it omits crystallographic anisotropy, temperature softening, strain-rate-insensitive yield strength, rate-dependent dislocation density, vacancy-assisted nucleation, and the MD condition matrix. Most importantly, it predicts deformation twinning, whereas the target explicitly reports no twinning. The stated boundary also overgeneralizes nanoscale nanopillar evidence to microscale FCC HEAs and moderately varied temperatures without direct support.
